title: Debrief: quantized matmul serialization causing bursty p99 regressions
content:
Summary:
We observed repeated customer SLO misses (p99 latency spikes) during short bursts of traffic starting 2026-05-08 21:14 UTC. The behavior affected hosted inference routes using int8 quantized model variants. Impacted customers experienced intermittent 5-20x increase in p99 latency for ~30s bursts while p50/p95 remained near-normal. No correctness errors were reported.

Customer escalation:
- First noisy report from Acme Commerce at 2026-05-08 21:20 UTC (support ticket #JIRA-RT-1123).
- Customer saw user-facing slowdown on a real-time summarization endpoint. They provided example request traces and timestamps.

Initial triage and scope:
- Alert: internal p99 alert triggered for hosted-api/region-us-west route at 21:18 UTC.
- Affected fleet: GPU hosts running a mix of A10s and A100s serving quantized int8 model shards.
- Traffic pattern: short bursts of concurrent small requests (prompt lengths 64-128 tokens) with sudden QPS increase from 70 -> 220 for ~20-45s.

Observed metrics (representative):
- Baseline p99: ~220ms; spike p99: ~1.1s (5x).
- Throughput: 18% drop in sustained tokens/sec during spikes.
- GPU SM util: transient decrease on A100 hosts (from 72% -> 48%) despite queue backlog.
- CPU sys time: small rise (6% -> 14%), notable increase in host-side kernel launch stalls.

What we ran to reproduce: 
1) Local microbench harness (bench-client) replay with identical prompt distribution and QPS ramp used by customer; reproduced p99 outliers in dev cluster when using the exact quantized checkpoint and runtime config.
2) nvprof/Nsight telemetry during replay: kernel timeline showed many short kernel launches serialized on the stream with repeated cudaStreamSynchronize-like stalls between matmul launches.
3) NVTX traces and perf counters: high number of kernel launches per request and low average kernel occupancy on tensor cores during crash windows.

Profiling findings / hypotheses tested: 
- Hypothesis A (kernel selection regression): A recent heuristic change in kernel selector (PR #3389) now prefers a tensor-core fused int8 matmul kernel for small-shape workloads. That kernel has a design that uses per-op synchronization and multiple small launches for tiling, which is efficient at high occupancy but serializes badly when request sizes are small and queueing is bursty.
  - Evidence: reverting the selector to the previous heuristic in a local build restored baseline p99 and smoothed launch patterns.
  - Corroborating artifact: flamegraph shows long gaps between kernel launches attributable to host-side CPU stalls waiting for previous kernel to finish.

- Hypothesis B (KV cache interaction): small sequence lengths were causing frequent KV cache misses and additional kernel/CPU synchronization in edge code paths.
  - Evidence: enabling prefix caching in the harness reduced some tail but did not fully mitigate spikes. Logs show extra cache population work but not at scale to account for 5x p99.

Root cause conclusion: 
The immediate root cause is a regression in the kernel selection heuristics that caused tensor-core-optimized int8 matmul kernels to be chosen for small-shape matmuls. Those kernels perform many fine-grained tiled launches and include synchronization points that serialize execution under bursty, low-latency request patterns. The serialization caused host-side stalls, lower SM utilization, and dramatic p99 tail effects even though average throughput and correctness remained acceptable.

Fix applied (hotfix):
- Short-term hotfix (deployed 2026-05-10 03:42 UTC): revert the heuristic in PR #3389 and add a guard that forces the legacy small-shape matmul path for shapes with M/N < 256 or effective sequence length < 128 for quantized int8 kernels.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 30 minutes, then 25% for 1 hour, then 100%. Canary metrics showed p99 returned to baseline within the first canary window.

Hotfix validation steps we followed: 
1) Unit and microbench:
   - Added regression microbench reproducing the pathological sequence of launches; verified new guard avoids tiled launches.
   - Confirmed p50/p95/p99 on bench-client with representative prompt mix before/after patch.
2) Instrumentation verification:
   - NVTX traces in canary hosts analyzed to confirm reduced inter-launch stalls.
   - Kernel launch counts per request dropped from ~18 -> ~4 on average.
3) Production canary:
   - 5% traffic, 30 min: observed p99 drop from 1.02s -> 0.23s. No increase in error rates.
   - 25% traffic, 60 min: stable.
   - Full rollout completed after no regressions seen.
4) Customer validation:
   - Sent canary data and timeline to Acme; they validated against their traces and confirmed improvement.

Why the regression slipped through: 
- The change passed functional tests and macro benchmarks (average throughput) but lacked a microbench for the small-shape int8 tiled-launch pattern.
- No explicit perf-gate for p99 tail under small prompt distributions existed at the time.

Action items (owner and ETA):
- eng-serving-runtime: add a microbench that reproduces the small-shape int8 tiled-launch scenario and include it in CI (owner: Liam Chen) — ETA 2026-05-26.
- eng-serving-runtime: add an automated perf regression check for p99 on a representative small-prompt workload to the PR gating pipeline (owner: Ayesha Patel) — ETA 2026-06-02.
- research/applied-ml: evaluate whether quantization layout changes could enable a single-launch fast path for small shapes (owner: Sofia Martinez) — ETA 2026-06-09.
- platform-engineering: create a dashboard comparing kernel launch counts and host-side launch latency aggregated by route/model (owner: Jonas Becker) — ETA 2026-05-20.
- release-eng: backfill a small-change rollback playbook for kernel selector regressions (owner: Renee O'Neill) — ETA 2026-05-18.

Postmortem notes / lessons learned:
- Microbench diversity matters: small-shape tiled kernels behave very differently than large-batch runs; ensure we cover the entire shape distribution seen in production.
- Perf gates should include tail metrics (p99/p999) and shape-aware scenarios to avoid regressions that only affect tail latency.
- Telemetry: track kernel launch counts and per-request launch latency as first-class metrics to surface serialization issues earlier.

Appendix (quick runbook for oncall):
1) If seeing p99 spike with normal p95/p50: check kernel launch counts and host-side kernel queueing metric.
2) If kernel selector suspected: try forcing legacy kernel path at runtime config (server flag: --force-small-int8-path) and observe p99.
3) For urgent customer impact: escalate to eng-serving-runtime lead and deploy canary revert, follow the canary rollout steps above.

Notes and references:
- PR with regression: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3389
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3396 (revert+guard)
- Customer ticket: JIRA-RT-1123
- Slack discussion: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1623435600000100

Open follow-ups:
- Confirm whether any Dedicated accounts with long prompt patterns were affected (investigate 2026-05-08 -> 2026-05-09 telemetry) — assigned to support (ETA 2026-05-14).
- Add regression dashboard alerts tied to kernel-launch anomalies (owner: platform-engineering, ETA 2026-05-20).

Status: hotfix deployed and validated; follow-up items tracked in JIRA.

Prepared by: Ayesha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
Reviewed by: Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez

End of debrief.
